stemMd:
For generations, gardeners in the dry valleys of the Orla region have planted squash beside a native shrub called saltbrush, believing that the shrub somehow helps the squash survive summer droughts. Botanist Delphine Arkwright decided to test the tradition. Over three summers, she grew squash in plots with and without neighboring saltbrush and measured the soil's moisture every day. The plots with saltbrush stayed noticeably damper, because the shrub's dense, low branches shaded the ground and slowed evaporation, and the squash in those plots produced nearly twice as much fruit. Arkwright concludes that the gardeners' practice rests on a real effect, even though they could not say how it worked.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Gardeners in the Orla region have stopped planting squash beside saltbrush because the shrub draws water out of the soil.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Arkwright's experiments showed that squash in the Orla region survives droughts better when it is shaded by tall trees.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Saltbrush grown in the Orla region produces more fruit when it is planted beside squash than when it is planted alone.

options.label: D
options.textMd: A botanist's experiments confirmed that a traditional gardening practice benefits squash and identified how it does so.

explanationMd:
A main-idea question asks for the point that the whole text is built to make, so trace its outline before reading the choices. The text opens with a tradition (planting squash beside saltbrush), says a botanist set out to test it, reports what she found (damper soil because the shrub shades the ground, and nearly twice the fruit), and ends with her conclusion that the tradition rests on a real effect.

A good summary has to cover both halves of what Arkwright did: she showed that the practice **works**, and she showed **why** it works (shade slows evaporation). The choice saying that a botanist's experiments confirmed a traditional practice and identified how it benefits squash does exactly that.

Check each wrong choice against a specific detail. The fruit that increased was the squash's, not the saltbrush's; nothing says gardeners have stopped the practice; and the shade came from a low shrub, not from tall trees.

distractorRationale.c: This swaps the two plants. The text says the squash planted beside saltbrush produced nearly twice as much fruit; it says nothing about fruit from the saltbrush itself.
distractorRationale.a: The text gives no sign that gardeners have abandoned the practice, and it reports the opposite of the stated reason: the saltbrush kept the soil damper rather than drying it out.
distractorRationale.b: This keeps the idea of shade but changes its source. The shade in Arkwright's plots came from the dense, low branches of saltbrush, a shrub; no trees are mentioned.

accessibilityText: A short science passage. Gardeners in the dry valleys of the Orla region have long planted squash beside a native shrub called saltbrush, believing it helps the squash survive summer droughts. Botanist Delphine Arkwright tested this over three summers, growing squash in plots with and without saltbrush and measuring soil moisture daily. Plots with saltbrush stayed damper because the shrub's dense, low branches shaded the ground and slowed evaporation, and squash there produced nearly twice as much fruit. Arkwright concludes that the practice rests on a real effect, though the gardeners could not say how it worked. The question asks for the main idea. The choices are: a botanist's experiments confirmed that a traditional gardening practice benefits squash and identified how it does so; saltbrush produces more fruit when planted beside squash than when planted alone; gardeners have stopped planting squash beside saltbrush because the shrub draws water out of the soil; and Arkwright's experiments showed that squash survives droughts better when shaded by tall trees.

provenance.notes: Original main-idea item. The Orla region, the saltbrush tradition and Arkwright's experiment are invented; distractors each distort one detail.
